review_notes: Read the full target (75 lines) and the definitions it builds on: `spectralPathDensity`, `spectralGroupPath`, `spectralGroupDiagonal` and their basic lemmas in `lean/OAI/Probability/InvariantIsing/Spectral/SpectralOverlapPaths.lean`, `OverlapPath`/`deficit` in `Core/Variational.lean`, and the project's `SpectralEntry` abbreviation in `Spectral/SpectralArrayGG.lean:14` together with the analogous packaging `cavityCanonicalDiagonal` in `Cavity/CavityCanonicalBlockLimit.lean:16`. I checked Mathlib's generic interval-projection API (`Set.projIcc`, `Set.IccExtend`, `Set.IccExtend_apply`, `continuous_projIcc`, `continuous_IccExtend_iff`, `Continuous.IccExtend`, `ContinuousMap.IccExtend`) and the interval-integral primitive lemmas used in the proofs. Candidates considered and rejected: (1) `cavityCanonicalCoordinate` is `Set.IccExtend zero_le_one (fun z : Icc 0 1 => ∫ r in 0..(z:ℝ), spectralPathDensity … r)` up to defeq, but the rubric explicitly allows named specialisations implemented through a generic map/composition, and the primitive of a particular density is not a Mathlib concept; (2) `cavityCanonicalLabel` returning `Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1` has no Mathlib counterpart (Mathlib's `unitInterval` is `Icc 0 1`, a different range, and the choice matches the project's `SpectralEntry`), and it is not the same concept as `SpectralEntry m`, which is a finite family of such labels; (3) `continuous_cavityCanonicalCoordinate`, `…_monotone`, `…_le_diagonal`, `…_nonneg` and `…_at_path` are either proof-level re-derivations (standalone theorem duplication, excluded by the rubric) or genuinely new facts about the project's spectral density. Degenerate cases: for `t ∉ Icc 0 1` the definition clamps through `projIcc`, so the coordinate is constant outside the unit interval (and the path identity lemma restricts to `p s`, which lies in `Icc 0 1` by `OverlapPath.nonneg`/`le_one`); the `-1` lower bound in the label range is never attained but is harmless since the coordinate is nonnegative. For `m = 0` the hypotheses are vacuous/inconsistent (`∑ a, ρ a = 1` over `Fin 0`), so no degenerate-instance issue arises. I found no avoidable competing reformulation of an existing Mathlib concept, so I abstain rather than report a weak finding. Remaining uncertainty: the rest of the large Cavity development was only spot-checked for an alternative definition of the same coordinate (none found; the only other uses of `Set.projIcc` under `OAI/Probability/InvariantIsing` are in the target file).
